topic_name: Subject, methods, development of the psyche, higher nervous activity and consciousness

1.question: The main method of psychology during the stage of the study of consciousness was considered to be...

options.E: Introspection with a description of experiences

2.question: Which limitation of early behaviorism made it difficult to explain different reactions to the same stimulus?

options.A: Rejection of the observation of behavior
options.B: Predominance of the analysis of self-reports
options.E: Exclusion of internal drives from analysis

3.question: The psyche as a form of reflection is defined primarily as...

options.A: A subjective image of the objective world
options.D: A system of acquired verbal designations
options.E: An objective copy of the subjective world

4.question: A researcher takes part in the work of a team and records interactions according to a pre-drawn plan. This is...

options.E: Participant everyday observation

5.question: A study not only records a quality but deliberately develops it by changing conditions. This is a(n)... experiment.

options.E: Ascertaining

6.question: Comparing the characterizations of one student written by several teachers independently of one another is...

options.E: Analysis of the products of activity

7.question: Studying the features of thinking from drawings made by a person belongs to the method of...

options.A: Analysis of the products of activity
options.E: The psychological conversation

8.question: Features that make it possible to distinguish an experiment from scientific observation:

options.A: An experiment necessarily requires a laboratory
options.C: An experiment involves active change of conditions by the researcher
options.D: Scientific observation excludes a preliminary plan
options.E: Observation studies the course of phenomena without intervention

9.question: To reveal the nature of a mental function, its development is traced from elementary forms to complex ones. The method used is the... method.

options.E: Introspective

10.question: Identify the statements that reflect real links between psychology and other sciences.

options.A: Physiology exhausts the content of psychology
options.B: Social history does not influence the psyche
options.C: Mental and somatic states influence each other
options.D: The design of technology takes human capabilities into account
options.E: Sign systems participate in the development of higher functions

11.question: In the activity-based explanation of the evolution of the psyche, the emergence of a new form of reflection is immediately preceded by...

options.E: An increase in the complexity of activity

12.question: Why does a higher position of an animal in zoological taxonomy not guarantee a more developed psyche?

options.A: All species have the same level of reflection
options.B: The psyche is determined by the number of conditioned reflexes
options.C: The environment determines the psyche independently of the organism
options.D: Mental development also depends on ecology and activity
options.E: Biological development is unrelated to morphology

13.question: The reflection of individual properties of stimuli corresponds to the stage of...

options.E: Verbal generalization

14.question: How does the stage of intellect differ from the perceptual stage in A. N. Leontiev's classification?

options.A: By the reflection of relations between objects
options.B: By the appearance of inherited reactions
options.C: By the emergence of a holistic image of an object
options.D: By the discrimination of separate qualities of a stimulus
options.E: By the first appearance of sensitivity

15.question: Characteristics that distinguish a skill from an instinct:

options.A: It is transmitted as a ready-made hereditary program
options.C: It does not change with repetition of the action
options.D: It is acquired in individual experience
options.E: It is consolidated through practice

16.question: Which statement is consistent with the systemic organization of higher mental functions?

options.A: The localization of a symptom is identical to the localization of the function
options.B: Participation of the cortex excludes participation of brainstem structures
options.C: The speech function is provided by the interaction of several brain regions
options.D: Each function is wholly contained in a single cortical center
options.E: Subcortical structures do not participate in complex functions

17.question: The specific stimulus of the second signal system is...

options.B: A sound regardless of its meaning
options.E: A word in its generalizing meaning

18.question: A child uses one word to generalize several varieties of an object. What indicates a transition to the second signal system?

options.A: The reaction is consolidated by reinforcement
options.B: The word is combined with a single procedure
options.C: A sound evokes an orienting reaction
options.E: Intonation acquires a conditioned meaning

19.question: In Pavlov's typology, the predominance of sensory images over verbal generalizations corresponds to the... type.

options.E: Strong inert

20.question: Properties of nervous processes that I. P. Pavlov took as the basis of the typology of higher nervous activity:

options.E: Dynamism

21.question: What distinguishes consciousness as a socio-historical form of the psyche?

options.A: Reflection of individual biologically significant properties
options.B: Preservation of traces of individual experience
options.C: Regulation of behavior by an immediate signal
options.D: Verbal mediation and purposeful transformation of the world
options.E: Formation of conditioned connections with the environment
Absence of mediation by speech

23.question: An experienced driver is aware of the route but performs the movements automatically. This shows that...

options.A: An automatic action is inaccessible to control
options.C: A skill turns a goal into an unconditioned reflex
options.D: Automatization eliminates the conscious regulation of activity
options.E: A conscious goal is compatible with automatized ways of acting

24.question: The speed with which excitation is replaced by inhibition characterizes the... of nervous processes.

options.E: Mobility

25.question: Which combination of features corresponds to a high level of conscious regulation?

options.B: Stimulus strength and involuntariness of response
options.C: Number of skills and absence of control
options.D: Vividness of sensations and speed of unconditioned reactions
options.E: A socially significant goal and control over the ways of acting
